caption: A loaded sled slides down a snowy slope, runs out onto a flat patch of bare grass, and stops within a short distance.

sa.check: A sled carrying a load is present on a snowy slope.
The sled slides down the slope.
The sled runs onto a patch of bare grass at the bottom and comes to a stop there.
The slope shows snow and the flat run-out shows grass: a visible change of surface.
The order is descent on snow, then grass, then stop.

pc.expect: On snow the sled keeps gliding; the sharp slowing begins where the runners reach the grass, and the sled stops within a short run on the grass.
pc.fail: The sled stops dead while still on the snow slope with nothing in its way; or glides across the grass without slowing, as if still on snow; or slows and then speeds up again on the flat.

pc.expect: The sled moves only downhill under gravity and stays stopped once it has stopped; it does not start, turn or restart untouched.
pc.fail: The sled sets off uphill; or turns sharply on open ground with nothing deflecting it; or moves again after having come to rest.

pc.expect: The sled keeps contact with the surface and its load rides on it; a hard stop may pitch the load forward but not upward or backward.
pc.fail: The sled floats above the snow or grass; or the load rises off the sled with nothing lifting it; or the load is thrown backward, uphill, when the sled stops.

pc.expect: Snow thrown up by the runners falls back to the ground; grass under the sled is flattened, not sprayed.
pc.fail: Snow spray hangs in the air or rises away; or the sled ploughs through the grass as if it were loose powder.
pc.precondition: Snow or grass is visibly disturbed by the runners.

pc.expect: One sled and its load keep their shape and number and stay above the ground.
pc.fail: The sled or its load vanishes, duplicates or changes into another object; or the sled passes through the ground or a fence.

pc.expect: The load's contents, the sled's colour and the boundary between snow and grass stay consistent throughout.
pc.fail: The load changes contents or colour; or the snow-grass boundary shifts between frames; or the slope changes shape.
